suggested_fix: Make get_current_counter() side-effect free in the fallback path: return CECallCounter() WITHOUT calling _current.set() when the var is unset. Better, fix propagation (copy_context at submit) so pool threads share the request's counter and never hit the fallback.

title: Per-thread CostExplorerClient cache keyed by id(session) leaks unboundedly and risks id reuse
description: get_ce_client caches a CostExplorerClient per worker thread in threading.local, keyed by key = id(session). get_session() returns a brand-new boto3.Session on every call (make_session constructs a fresh Session each time), so every request produces a new session object with a new id. The cache dict _ce_local.clients never evicts. Each cached value is a CostExplorerClient that holds a reference to that session and its boto3 'ce' client, so the session can never be garbage-collected while the entry lives -> the per-thread dict grows by one permanent entry (session + boto3 client + botocore session/endpoint state) for every request handled by that thread. Over a long-running server this is an unbounded memory leak proportional to total requests, multiplied by the number of worker threads. Separately, the 'cache by id(session)' design is unsound in principle: if a session ever WERE freed, id() is aggressively reused (verified ~99.98% reuse among ephemeral objects), so a future session could collide with a stale entry and silently reuse a client bound to a different (already-closed) session/credentials.
scenario: A dashboard left running for days serving thousands of summary/services/trend requests across several profiles. Each request makes a new session; get_ce_client adds a never-evicted entry per worker thread. RSS climbs continuously with no upper bound; eventually OOM. The leak is invisible at low traffic, which is exactly when it escapes testing.
suggested_fix: Don't key by id() of a per-request object. Either (a) cache the CostExplorerClient on the session/profile itself (e.g. a WeakValueDictionary keyed by profile name, or attach to the session) so it lives and dies with the session, or (b) reuse one session per profile (memoized) instead of constructing a fresh Session per request, or (c) just construct the client per call (boto3 client creation is cheap relative to a CE network round-trip) and drop the cache entirely.

title: SqliteCache opens a new connection per operation and never closes it
description: Every get/get_swr/set/bust calls self._connect() which does sqlite3.connect(...) (plus two PRAGMA statements) and wraps it in `with self._connect() as conn:`. The context-manager form of a sqlite3 Connection only commits/rolls back the transaction; it does NOT close the connection (verified: connection is still usable after the with-block). So each cache operation allocates a fresh OS-level SQLite connection with its own WAL/SHM file handles and only releases them on garbage collection/finalization, not deterministically. cache_get/cache_set are called on the hot path of every cost route (often multiple times per request) and from the acu-refresh and per-request ThreadPoolExecutor workers concurrently. Under load this is unbounded connection/file-descriptor churn: many simultaneously-open connections, each opening WAL handles, with the additional cost of running PRAGMA journal_mode/synchronous on every single op.
scenario: A large account whose pages trigger many cache_get/cache_set calls per request, served at high concurrency by uvicorn workers plus the 4-thread refresh pool. Open SQLite connections accumulate faster than GC reclaims them; the process approaches its file-descriptor ulimit and starts failing with 'unable to open database file' or 'database is locked' (timeout=5.0 is short), turning cache reads into 500s.
suggested_fix: Maintain one connection per thread (threading.local) opened once and reused, or explicitly close the connection in a try/finally after each op (conn.close()). Run the PRAGMAs once at connection creation, not per operation. Consider a single shared connection guarded by the existing lock since writes are already serialized.

title: Nested ThreadPoolExecutors + per-region session/client creation cause thread and connection explosion at region/service scale
description: enumerate_all opens an outer ThreadPoolExecutor (up to 16 workers) and submits ~7 service jobs. Six of those jobs (RDS, EIP, ELB, Lambda, S3, DynamoDB) each call _fanout_regions, which itself opens a NEW inner ThreadPoolExecutor(min(12, len(regions))) and submits one task per region, each task calling _frozen_session(session, reg) to construct a brand-new boto3.Session and then one or more boto3 service clients. With N regions this is N fresh Sessions + clients per service per call: e.g. 20 regions x 7 enumerated services = ~140 freshly-built boto3 Sessions and at least that many clients per single enumerate_all invocation, plus EBS which builds a session per region and the downstream per-resource N+1 calls (lambda list_tags per fn, dynamodb describe_table + list_tags_of_resource per table, elb describe_tags/describe_target_health per LB/TG). Concurrent inner pools across ~6 service jobs can hold roughly 6 x 12 = 72 inner worker threads plus the outer pool plus EBS, all at once. Building a boto3 Session/client is not cheap (it parses config, builds endpoint resolvers); doing it ~150 times per enumeration multiplies CPU and memory and floods the SDK with concurrent connection setup.
scenario: An organization opted into many regions (e.g. 25+) with thousands of resources. A resources page that calls enumerate_all spins up dozens of nested threads and well over a hundred boto3 sessions/clients in a burst, spiking memory and thread count and triggering throttling on describe APIs; if enumerate_all is itself invoked from another pool worker (via attribute_resources_via_describe), the nesting compounds and can starve the outer pool.
suggested_fix: Use a single bounded executor with (region x service) tasks rather than nesting per-service inner pools, so total concurrency is capped once. Cache/reuse one frozen Session per region (build N sessions, not N x services) and reuse clients across services in the same region. Cap total worker threads explicitly regardless of region count.

title: Forecast metric translation falls through to CamelCase for unmapped metrics, breaking get_cost_forecast
description: get_forecast translates the metric to the SNAKE_CASE form CE's forecast API requires via a dict .get(metric.value, metric.value). For any CostMetric value not in the map (e.g. a BLENDED or any future metric whose .value isn't a key), it falls back to metric.value, which is the CamelCase get_cost_and_usage form (e.g. 'BlendedCost' is mapped, but 'UsageQuantity' or any other enum member would pass through as-is). get_cost_forecast then rejects it with a ValidationException, returning None silently (the except swallows it and logs a warning). This is minor today because callers use UNBLENDED, but the silent fallback hides the misuse.
scenario: A future caller passes a CostMetric whose .value is not one of the five mapped strings; the forecast silently returns None and the summary card shows no forecast, with only a generic warning in the logs and no indication the metric name was the cause.
suggested_fix: Raise/log explicitly when the metric is not in the forecast-metric map instead of passing the CamelCase value through to the API, or derive the SNAKE_CASE form generically from the enum.
